newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Top Philippine businessman welcomes peso plunge.
newsitem.headline: Top Philippine businessman welcomes peso plunge.

text.p: A top Philippine businessman welcomed Friday's effective devaluation of the peso, saying efforts to prop it up had become unsustainable.
"We're pleased that the Central Bank decided to allow free market forces to come in," president of the Federation of Philippine Industry Raul Concepcion told Reuters Financial Television.
After the Central Bank said it would allow the peso to move in a wider range against the dollar, it fell just over 11 percent before Philippine banks stopped trading the currency.
"They couldn't continue to defend with high overnight interest rates," he said.

The Central Bank has spent an estimated more than $1 billion over the past four days to beat off speculation but, more worrying to local businessmen, it also pushed overnight interest rates to 2-1/2 year highs of 32 percent.
"This move is good in the sense that we will go more on the market determined forces," he said.
